features.name: second_person_word_share
features.definition: What proportion of all words across the counter-argument comments are second-person words (you, your and their variants)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as JSON list of strings; if missing/malformed return null; if empty list or zero total words return null. Lowercase each comment; tokenize words with re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text) (curly apostrophes normalized to '). Count tokens matching ^(you|your|yours|yourself|yourselves)$ or you're/you've/you'll/you'd. Result = total matched tokens across all comments / total tokens across all comments. Mechanical count over raw text, including quoted text and any outcome announcements; no semantic filtering.

h0: second_person_word_share has no association with whether the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher second_person_word_share in counter-arguments is associated with higher likelihood of delta.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view); association only, not causal. Operational assumptions: 'more second-person language' is measured as the share of words (rate, not raw count) pooled across all available counter-comments, including you-contractions and yours/yourself. Quoted OP text within comments is counted mechanically, as are possible delta announcements in raw text, so contamination is possible. Comment order/timing unknown; comments may be by repeated commenters; available comments may include later replies.
